provenance.notes: Mid-size design-build firm with in-house designers, project managers and crews on whole-home remodels, additions and villa renovations. Leaned on the paid design phase, lead qualification and a client portal. Portal and integration ranges depend on their project management system and are set wide.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What the design agreement covers, measured drawings, design concepts, selections, a fixed construction price at the end, the fee and how it is credited if they build
pageStructurePlus.why: Serious clients want to know what they get before committing to design. Explaining the design agreement filters out people shopping for free drawings.

pageStructurePlus.section: Whole-home, addition and villa renovation projects
pageStructurePlus.contains: A page per project type with typical scope, duration ranges, permit and engineering steps, investment ranges and finished projects of that type
pageStructurePlus.why: A couple planning an addition doesn't want to scroll bathrooms. Project-type pages match how large remodel buyers search and compare.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Profiles of the in-house designers, project managers and lead carpenters, who the client meets at each stage, and how one firm owns design and construction
pageStructurePlus.why: Design-build buyers are choosing the people they'll live with for months. Seeing the team and the single point of contact is the decision.

pageStructurePlus.section: Phasing, living at home and move-out planning
pageStructurePlus.contains: How the firm phases a whole-home renovation, which rooms stay usable, when a family should move out, dust and access control, and weekly site meetings
pageStructurePlus.why: Families with children or pets decide whether a large remodel is even possible based on this. Answering it early keeps them in the pipeline.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What clients see once they sign: schedule, selections with deadlines, change orders to approve, payment milestones and weekly progress notes
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers fear surprise costs and silence. Showing the portal before they sign proves the firm runs projects with documents, not phone calls.

pageStructurePlus.section: Careers for designers, project managers and carpenters
pageStructurePlus.contains: Open roles by team, how projects are staffed, training, tools and vehicles provided, pay ranges they choose to publish, and a short application
pageStructurePlus.why: Project managers and skilled carpenters cap how many renovations the firm can run. They compare firms on organisation before applying.

designDirections.name: Qualified Enquiry
designDirections.bestFor: Design-build firms whose first need is an enquiry form that asks budget, scope and timing before a meeting
designDirections.headlineSample: Design-build remodeling in {City}, from first sketch to keys
designDirections.whyItFits: Butter & Denim's warm cream and geometric headings feel approachable for families, while staying plain enough for a budget question up front.

designDirections.name: Project Library
designDirections.bestFor: Firms with a deep portfolio of additions and whole-home renovations, filtered by project type and investment
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo fails contrast. Gallery White lets large project photography lead, and its Didone headings give finished renovations a magazine feel.

designDirections.name: Design-Build Atelier
designDirections.bestFor: Established firms selling high-budget renovations and villa remodels through a paid design phase
designDirections.headlineSample: One team to design and build your {City} home
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy & Brass reads like an architect's practice: dark, calm and expensive, with an editorial serif that suits a paid design agreement.

openers.line: Your renovation galleries are beautiful but took a long time to load on my phone. Couples browse additions on the sofa at night and give up on a heavy remodel page.
openers.hook: Open their portfolio page on a phone over mobile data. Note roughly how long the first project takes to appear.
openers.linkLine: The same renovation portfolio, fast on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your enquiry form asks for a name and a message and nothing about budget, scope or timing. Your designers must spend first meetings on remodel enquiries that were never a fit.
openers.hook: Open their contact or start-a-project form and list the fields. If there's no budget, project type or timing question, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A design-build enquiry form that qualifies before the meeting: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your portfolio mixes additions, whole-home renovations and bathrooms in one scroll. Someone planning a second storey has to dig to find the work that matches their project.
openers.hook: Check whether their projects can be filtered by type, size or investment. Note the project types you can see.
openers.linkLine: A renovation portfolio filtered by project type: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site says you're design-build but doesn't explain the paid design phase: what it covers, what it costs, and how it credits toward construction. Serious clients look for that before they call.
openers.hook: Look for 'design agreement', 'design retainer' or 'process' on their site. Note whether fees or deliverables are mentioned.
openers.linkLine: The design-build process and design agreement, explained: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Design studio visits by phone only
openers.line: You have a design studio people can visit, but booking a time there means a phone call during work hours. Remodel clients plan this in the evening.
openers.hook: Find their showroom or studio address on the listing, then check the site for any way to book a visit online.

openers.line: I've seen your posts hiring a renovation project manager and carpenters, and the site has no careers page. Good project managers judge a design-build firm's organisation before they apply.
openers.hook: Find a current job post for a PM, designer or carpenter and note the date. Check the site for a careers link.
openers.linkLine: A careers section for designers, PMs and carpenters: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews keep naming the project manager who answered every question during months of renovation. That's what large remodel buyers worry about, and it's not on the site.
openers.hook: Copy one review line that names a designer or project manager. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Client reviews beside each renovation project: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've posted about recent remodeling recognition, and the site doesn't mention it. People comparing design-build firms for a large renovation weigh exactly that.
openers.hook: Only if they posted an award, feature or association recognition. Note the name and year, and use it only as published.
openers.linkLine: Your design-build recognition next to the project gallery: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts show home additions and second-storey builds, but the site only lists kitchens and baths. Families outgrowing their house search for additions and find someone else.
openers.hook: Scroll their posts for additions, extensions or whole-floor renovations, then check the services list.
openers.linkLine: A home addition page with finished projects: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your renovation projects are spread across {Neighborhood} and several nearby towns, but the site names only {City}. People search remodeler plus their town and miss you.
openers.hook: List the towns or communities named in their project posts and reviews, then check for area pages.
openers.linkLine: Renovation pages for each town you build in: {demo-link}

openers.line: A whole-home renovation is a big decision about money. If your clients pay in milestones or use renovation financing, explaining it on the site keeps them from waiting another year.
openers.hook: Only if they mention payment schedules or financing anywhere. Never name a lender.
openers.linkLine: A remodel investment and payment page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Clients hand a design-build firm their house for months. Your licence, insurance and workmanship warranty belong on the renovation pages, not only on the contract.
openers.hook: Look for licence numbers or warranty wording on their listing, trucks or site. Use only what they publish, in [brackets] on the demo.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and warranty on every renovation page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like much of your remodel work comes from architects, agents and past clients. Even referred families study the design-build process online before the first meeting.
openers.hook: Look for mentions of architects, interior designers or agents in their posts or reviews. Name one partner type.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred renovation client should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Renovations that start early next year get designed in the months before. The families signing design agreements now are deciding between firms this season.
openers.hook: Use in the last third of the year. Check for posts about booking design for next year.
openers.linkLine: Book next year's renovation design now: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted shows the whole design-build story: plans, crew and the finished rooms. It deserves a full case page, not a short post.
openers.hook: Pick their newest large project: an addition, a villa renovation, a whole floor. Name it.
openers.linkLine: That renovation as a full case page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — I've been looking at the renovation projects {Business Name} has posted, and the work is excellent.

The site doesn't explain the paid design phase, the portfolio isn't sorted by project type, and the enquiry form doesn't ask budget or timing. I've put together a sample that does all three, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it be useful if I sent it to you or whoever handles marketing?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a portfolio filtered by project type, a design-phase page, team profiles, a client portal preview and an enquiry form that asks budget, scope and timing. Happy to walk you and your design lead through it in fifteen minutes.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}. I build websites and client portals for design-build remodeling firms. I sent a sample site for {Business Name} last week, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"Short version: a renovation portfolio filtered by project type, the design phase explained, team profiles and an enquiry form that qualifies on budget and timing, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Who else should see it?"

IF YES:
"What did you and your designers think?"
 → let them talk, then ask: "How many first meetings a month turn out not to be a fit?"
"The site runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, project updates and reporting. For your firm I'd expect about {Build Price}. A client portal and a connection to your project management system are quoted separately."
"Can we get thirty minutes with you and your design lead next week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a scope with the site first and the portal as phase two, so you can approve them separately."

objections.objection: We don't publish prices, every project is custom.
objections.handler: "Then publish investment ranges by project type and say the fixed price comes from the design phase. The form asks budget privately. It filters out the free-drawings crowd without quoting anyone."

objections.objection: Our project management software already has a client portal.
objections.handler: "Good, then we connect to it. The site shows a preview of it so buyers see you're organised, and signed clients land in the system you already use."
"Then the site's job is choosing better clients, not more of them. Budget and timing questions up front mean your designers spend first meetings on the right renovations."

objections.objection: Most of our work comes from architects and referrals.
objections.handler: "Referred families still look you up before the first meeting. The design-phase page and the team profiles turn a name they were given into a firm they trust."

objections.objection: I need to run it past my partner and our design lead.
objections.handler: "Of course. I'll send a short recording of the sample and a one-page scope, and I'm happy to meet the three of you."
"The site is {Build Range}, about {Build Price} for your firm, plus {Care Range} a month. One signed renovation covers it many times over. The portal is quoted after I see your systems."

email.subject: Renovation portfolio and design phase for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build renovation portfolios, design-phase pages and client portals for design-build firms, and I made a sample for {Business Name}. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm clearing out sample sites this week, including the {Business Name} renovation one with the design-phase page and filtered portfolio.

Should I keep it up for your partner or design lead? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — families planning renovations for next year are signing design agreements around now in {City}. Thought of you.

The sample with the design-phase page and filtered portfolio is still here: {demo-link}. Same scope and price whenever the timing suits.

bullets: Peg the build to one signed renovation; a single whole-home project is worth many times the site.
Price the portfolio by project count and case pages, not by page count.
Quote the site and the client portal as separate phases; the portal depends on their project management system.
The enquiry qualifier and design-phase page are the core; price everything around reducing wasted first meetings.
Investment ranges come from the firm's own past projects and are signed off by them; never invent a range.
Never publish a licence, award or warranty term they haven't; leave a bracketed slot.

lineItems.description: Max with plans, the brief, phase photos, the team who ran it, duration and a client quote approved in writing.
Max with budget, scope, timing and address questions, scoring, and routing to the right designer with a booked call.

lineItems.item: Portfolio filter by project type and investment
lineItems.description: Max when filters cover project type, size, style and investment band, and the firm can tag new projects themselves.
Max when it books into each designer's calendar, sends a preparation guide and collects inspiration photos first.
Max when each page shows projects in that town, local permit notes and the housing styles common there.
Max with a profile per designer, PM and lead carpenter, their projects linked, and a short video introduction each.
Max with roles by team, project staffing explained and applicant routing to the right manager.

lineItems.item: Speed and accessibility pass on the old site
lineItems.description: Max when large galleries need image compression, alt text, heading order and contrast fixes across many pages.

whatElseYouSell.name: Professional renovation photo and video days
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A photographer at each finished renovation, plus short walk-through clips, so every case page has proper twilight and detail shots."

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for the design studio
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Weekly posts of renovation progress and finished rooms on the studio listing, with questions answered, so the firm shows up as an active design-build team."

whatElseYouSell.name: Handover review and testimonial programme
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "At each renovation handover, clients are asked for a review and a short written testimonial about the design process, with written consent to quote them."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 1, timed to the next handover.

whatElseYouSell.name: Long-cycle nurture for future renovations
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Enquiries that aren't ready yet get a monthly note with one finished renovation and one planning tip, so they come back when they're ready to design."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the qualifying form produces not-yet leads.

whatElseYouSell.name: Finished-home open house events
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "With the homeowner's permission, a private tour of a finished whole-home renovation for qualified prospects and referral partners, invitations and follow-up included."
whatElseYouSell.when: Twice a year, after a standout handover.

whatElseYouSell.name: Architect and agent referral kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short design-build capability document and a referral page for architects and agents, showing how the firm handles their clients' renovations."

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite fence banners and signage
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Fence banners and site boards on every renovation that match the new site, so the neighbours watching the build know who to call."
whatElseYouSell.when: After launch, on the next project start.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly enquiry quality report
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One page a month: renovation enquiries by project type, budget band and source, and how many became design agreements."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, after a full month of qualified form data.

whatElseYouSell.name: Design-led social content plan
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Weekly posts that follow one renovation from design concept to handover, written with the designers, so followers see the process the firm sells."

withoutAI.route: Architects and structural engineers they collaborate with
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The structural engineer who signs off your additions shows nothing online but a phone number. A practice site with project types is a quick build for me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Engineers and architects trust the design-build firm that builds their drawings well, and they rarely have time for their own site.

withoutAI.route: Furniture and decor studios their clients buy from
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The furniture studio your clients visit after every renovation still sells from a showroom only. An online catalogue with appointments would bring them more."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Studios want renovation clients at the moment they furnish, and the remodeler is the one who sends them.

withoutAI.route: Landscape design firms finishing the outside
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The landscape designer who finishes the garden after your additions shows projects only on social media. A portfolio site is the next build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Remodel clients ask the remodeler who to use outside, so the referral and the trust are already there.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The glazing supplier you order from for every renovation takes quotes by email. A product configurator with trade pricing logins would save their counter time."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers value their biggest trade accounts, and an introduction from one carries weight.

withoutAI.whoPays: The installer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The audio-visual installer who wires your whole-home renovations sells by word of mouth. A project site with room-by-room packages is quick."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Both firms work the same houses at the same time, so referrals already pass both ways.

withoutAI.route: Real estate agents selling renovated homes
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agent who lists homes you've renovated shows them with plain listing copy. A listing site that tells the renovation story would sell them better."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents who refer renovation clients want the same firm's polish on their own listings.

withAI.route: Drawing set summariser for structural engineers
withAI.pitchLine: "Each incoming renovation drawing set gets a summary of beams, openings and load changes for the engineer to check, before the first site visit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Engineers review remodel drawings constantly, and the design-build client gets faster sign-offs.

withAI.route: Room styling assistant for furniture studios
withAI.whoPays: The furniture or decor studio, monthly
withAI.pitchLine: "Renovation clients upload their new room's plan and finishes, and the studio gets a draft furniture list that fits before the appointment."
withAI.whyItWorks: Studios convert better with a prepared list, and the remodeler's clients get a smoother finish.

withAI.route: Planting plan drafter for landscape firms
withAI.pitchLine: "The landscape designer drops in the new addition's footprint and site notes, and gets a draft planting and hardscape outline to refine."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small landscape firms spend evenings on drafts; the handoff from the remodel already includes the footprint.

withAI.route: Quote request assistant for glazing suppliers
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors send window schedules in any format, and the supplier gets a structured quote request with sizes and specs to confirm."
withAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers retype schedules from many remodelers; the design-build client gets quotes back faster.

withAI.pitchLine: "Renovation clients answer a few questions about rooms and habits, and the installer gets a recommended wiring and equipment package to quote."
withAI.whyItWorks: Wiring decisions have to be made early in a renovation, so both firms benefit from a faster answer.

withAI.pitchLine: "Agents enter what was renovated and when, and get draft listing copy that explains the remodel accurately, for them to edit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents write listings weekly, and the remodeler gets credited on every renovated home they sell.

softwareAI.name: Enquiry auto-reply with project-type guide
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every renovation enquiry gets an instant reply with the investment guide for their project type and a link to book a call with a designer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1. Needs the qualifying form live, investment guides they approve and designer calendars.

softwareAI.name: Design meeting prep sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before the first design meeting, clients get a short questionnaire, a request for inspiration photos and a note on what to bring, so the designer arrives prepared."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the questionnaire, meeting types and the design team's checklist.

softwareAI.name: Lead qualifier connected to their CRM
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each renovation enquiry is scored on budget, scope and timing and lands in your CRM assigned to the right designer, with notes already filled."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs CRM access, scoring rules from the design lead and a test record.

softwareAI.name: Website assistant for renovation questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'how does the design phase work' and 'how long does an addition take' from your own process pages, then books a call with a designer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the process pages, investment ranges and designer calendars. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for finished renovations
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a client reviews their finished addition, a thank-you that mentions their project and their PM is drafted for the owner to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs listing access and a short tone guide. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Discovery call brief writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After the first call, the designer gets a written design brief: rooms, wishes, budget, constraints and open questions, ready for the design agreement."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs recorded calls with client consent and the brief template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Design agreement and proposal builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Designers assemble the design agreement from the brief with scope, fee and deliverables, and the client signs and pays the design fee online."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their agreement template, fee rules and the payment setup.

softwareAI.name: Renovation client portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients log in to see the renovation schedule, selections due, change orders to approve, milestone payments and weekly progress photos."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4 to month 6. Needs the project management system's data access, document templates and payment setup.

softwareAI.name: Scope drafter from site walkthrough notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A PM talks through an existing house room by room, and gets a draft renovation scope with trades, allowances and questions for the estimator."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past scopes and estimates and an estimator review step. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Weekly client update writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Project managers' site notes and photos become a friendly weekly renovation update for each client, reviewed by the PM before it goes out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the portal. Needs PM notes from a few projects and the tone they want. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Selections board with deadlines
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every finish, fixture and appliance per room with allowance, chosen item, order date and lead time, so no renovation stalls waiting for a decision."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the selections list format, allowance rules and supplier lead times.

softwareAI.name: Change order approval and payment flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Change orders go out with the drawing, price and schedule impact, get signed on a phone and trigger the payment request, with reminders if they sit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the change order template, approval rules and the payment setup.

softwareAI.name: Project budget-versus-actual dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each renovation's estimate, committed costs, change orders and margin on one screen, so leadership sees which project types make money."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs estimates and cost exports from their accounting and project systems.

softwareAI.name: Trade partner portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Subcontractors see their renovation schedule, drawings and site notes, confirm dates and upload invoices and insurance certificates in one place."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs the trade partner list, document requirements and schedule data.

softwareAI.name: Designer and PM applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for design, project manager and carpentry roles answer role questions and share portfolios, and the hiring manager gets a ranked shortlist."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any month they're hiring. Needs must-haves per role and pay bands. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: After-hours renovation enquiry assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Evening callers planning a remodel are asked about project type, budget and timing, and booked straight into a designer's next free call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs designer calendars and the qualifying questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Warranty request portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Past clients log a warranty item with a photo and room, the service team schedules it, and the anniversary walkthrough is booked automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs warranty terms, the past client list and the service team's calendar.

softwareAI.name: Portfolio tagger for new projects
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a finished renovation's photos and the tool suggests rooms, style and features for the portfolio filters, for the marketing lead to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the filtered portfolio. Needs the tag list and a batch of tagged projects. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Permit and inspection milestone reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each renovation's permit submissions, inspections and approvals are tracked, with reminders to the PM before a missed inspection delays the trades."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs the permit steps where they build and the project schedule.

softwareAI.name: Estimating cost library
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Unit costs from past renovations by trade and finish level, so estimators price a new addition from real numbers instead of a fresh spreadsheet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs a year of estimates and actual costs and the estimator's structure.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the client portal for design-build firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a renovation client portal for one design-build firm. Every firm running long projects fields the same 'what's happening this week' calls."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the selections, change order and update workflow every design-build firm shares.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members get a design-build site template with process, investment and team pages, plus the qualifying form, at a member rate."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need member benefits and want members to look professional; one agreement reaches many firms.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Building supply dealers' pro contractor programme
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer your pro remodeling accounts a selections board and client portal that orders through you, and they keep buying from your yard."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Dealers compete for pro accounts; a tool that sits inside the remodeler's workflow beats a discount.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each franchisee needs territory renovation pages, a qualifying form and a portal under one brand. Build once, copy per territory."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Franchisors want consistency and speed for new territories; the build already exists and runs on a live firm.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The developer or community operator, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Owners in your communities request approved renovation packages and see the permit steps, with vetted design-build firms quoting on one portal."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Master developers want renovations controlled and approved; the design-build client becomes a preferred partner.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency sends ad traffic to remodeling sites that can't qualify an enquiry. License my design-phase pages and qualifying form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client relationship; you sell the part that turns traffic into design agreements.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Borrowers with renovation loans choose vetted design-build firms, see draw schedules and upload progress photos for each release."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Lenders need trustworthy contractors and progress evidence; the portal already tracks milestones.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every renovation across your portfolio on one board: scope, budget, change orders and handover dates, with the design-build team posting updates."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Investors run many renovations at once and need visibility; the dashboard is already built.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Students learn a real design-build workflow on case studies from live renovations, with permission from the firm and its clients."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools want industry-connected material, and the remodeler gains a hiring pipeline.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Cabinetry and millwork manufacturers' dealer pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each design-build dealer of your cabinetry gets project pages featuring your product and a qualified renovation enquiry form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers want dealers to present them well; the case page system already exists.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same design-build system in the next region
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A non-competing design-build firm in another region
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one design-build firm per region, and {City} is taken. The next region is open, and the portal is ready."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the portal, the qualifier and the case study.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The firm with an unfinished build
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Paid for a renovation client portal or selections tool that never launched? I've shipped that exact build for a design-build firm."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded buyers already decided to spend and want someone who has finished one.

upsellLadder.line: "The renovation site and the care plan are one contract, so a new case page or team member is one message to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Professional renovation photo and video days
upsellLadder.trigger: The next handover is booked and the portfolio has placeholder slots.
upsellLadder.line: "Your next renovation handover is the best case page you'll get this season. Let's shoot it properly."

upsellLadder.offer: Lead qualifier connected to their CRM
upsellLadder.trigger: Two months of form data show how many remodel enquiries miss on budget or timing.
upsellLadder.line: "Your designers are still sorting enquiries by hand. Let the remodel enquiries arrive scored and assigned."

upsellLadder.trigger: Qualified leads wait days for a design agreement to be written.
upsellLadder.line: "Good renovation clients wait days for the design agreement. Let them sign and pay the design fee the day after the call."

upsellLadder.trigger: PMs mention evening calls and texts from clients asking about selections and schedule.
upsellLadder.line: "Your PMs answer the same renovation questions every evening. The portal answers them before the client picks up the phone."

upsellLadder.trigger: The portal is live and PMs struggle to keep weekly updates going.
upsellLadder.line: "Your PMs already take site notes. Let those notes become the weekly renovation update automatically."

upsellLadder.trigger: Leadership asks which project types made money this year.
upsellLadder.line: "You have a year of renovations in the system. The dashboard shows which project types to chase next year."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first anniversary walkthroughs of renovations come due.
upsellLadder.line: "Your first clients are due their anniversary walkthrough. A warranty portal turns them into your next referrals."
